findings.detail: The long focuses on the mismatch between the title and an NBC report, details what the order did and did not authorize, and concludes that the title or source record needs correction. This is an audit of the record rather than a reader-facing description of the press-funding order it actually describes.

The long repeats the medium and supplied context almost verbatim, including the fundraiser, cancer claim, bird statement, expert response, and later repetition. It adds only a general caveat separating health claims from legitimate noise and wildlife questions, without further context about the speech or its reception.
Both medium and long are null. The supplied context describes the revised 2017 travel restrictions and their court challenges, but the entry provides no reader-facing summary or explanation.

The long calls 18,000 a “record low,” but the supplied synopsis and linked White House determination identify the cap without supporting that historical comparison. The added claim needs a sourced comparison or removal.

The long says the “draft describes” conditions and that “the entry records” concerns, then tells readers which conclusions should not be inferred. Those packet references and audit directions interrupt the account of the transfers and reported prison conditions.

The long identifies what the Reuters report supports, says it does not document the broader visa claims, and instructs that those claims need separate evidence. This source-mismatch note should not be embedded in the description of the H-2A rule change.

The long refers directly to the “existing title” and instructs that its count not be repeated without a source, then discusses what the episode does and does not establish. This is correction guidance rather than reader-facing context about the OSC recommendation and Trump’s response.
